{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793047696582,"sessionID":"ses_e8609575affeVu0Ptqg56NiOxK","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01TTkv1p8whT5hhpeb42ENjj","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/matmul_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_hybrid_r3/matmul/matmul.cpp","content":"#include <mpi.h>\n#include <omp.h>\n#include <cuda_runtime.h>\n\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <chrono>\n#include <cmath>\n#include <cstdio>\n#include <cstdlib>\n#include <cstring>\n#include <vector>\n\n#include \"../common/results_output.hpp\"\n\n// Hybrid parallelization:\n//   MPI    - rows of A/C are block-distributed across ranks (one rank per GPU or GPU group).\n//   OpenMP - one host thread per GPU owned by a rank; also parallelizes matrix initialization.\n//   CUDA   - tiled double-precision GEMM kernel on each device.\n//\n// Every C(i,j) is still accumulated sequentially over k = 0..N-1, so results are\n// bit-identical to the original serial triple loop.\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);                                         \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\n// Fill rows [rowBegin, rowBegin + rowCount) of an N-column matrix (OpenMP parallel).\nvoid initRows(double* mat, const size_t N, const size_t rowBegin, const size_t rowCount) {\n    #pragma omp parallel for schedule(static)\n    for (size_t r = 0; r < rowCount; ++r) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[r * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, rowBegin + r, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Tiled GEMM: C[M x N] = A[M x N] * B[N x N], all row-major.\n// Block tile 64x64, k-tile 16, 16x16 threads, each thread computes a 4x4 register tile.\n// Each output element accumulates over k in ascending order (same as the serial reference).\nconstexpr int BM = 64;\nconstexpr int BN = 64;\nconstexpr int BK = 16;\nconstexpr int TM = 4;\nconstexpr int TN = 4;\n\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(256)\nmatmulTiled(const double* __restrict__ A, const double* __restrict__ B,\n            double* __restrict__ C, const int M, const int N) {\n    __shared__ double As[BM][BK + 1];\n    __shared__ double Bs[BK][BN + 1];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int tid = ty * blockDim.x + tx;\n    const int rowBase = blockIdx.y * BM;\n    const int colBase = blockIdx.x * BN;\n\n    double acc[TM][TN];\n    #pragma unroll\n    for (int m = 0; m < TM; ++m)\n        #pragma unroll\n        for (int n = 0; n < TN; ++n)\n            acc[m][n] = 0.0;\n\n    for (int kt = 0; kt < N; kt += BK) {\n        const int kl = min(BK, N - kt);\n\n        for (int idx = tid; idx < BM * BK; idx += 256) {\n            const int r = idx / BK;\n            const int c = idx % BK;\n            const int gr = rowBase + r;\n            As[r][c] = (gr < M && c < kl)\n                           ? A[static_cast<size_t>(gr) * N + kt + c]\n                           : 0.0;\n        }\n        for (int idx = tid; idx < BK * BN; idx += 256) {\n            const int r = idx / BN;\n            const int c = idx % BN;\n            const int gc = colBase + c;\n            Bs[r][c] = (r < kl && gc < N)\n                           ? B[static_cast<size_t>(kt + r) * N + gc]\n                           : 0.0;\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        for (int kk = 0; kk < kl; ++kk) {\n            double a[TM];\n            double b[TN];\n            #pragma unroll\n            for (int m = 0; m < TM; ++m) a[m] = As[ty * TM + m][kk];\n            #pragma unroll\n            for (int n = 0; n < TN; ++n) b[n] = Bs[kk][tx * TN + n];\n            #pragma unroll\n            for (int m = 0; m < TM; ++m)\n                #pragma unroll\n                for (int n = 0; n < TN; ++n)\n                    acc[m][n] += a[m] * b[n];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    #pragma unroll\n    for (int m = 0; m < TM; ++m) {\n        const int gr = rowBase + ty * TM + m;\n        if (gr >= M) continue;\n        #pragma unroll\n        for (int n = 0; n < TN; ++n) {\n            const int gc = colBase + tx * TN + n;\n            if (gc < N) C[static_cast<size_t>(gr) * N + gc] = acc[m][n];\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// Block partition of `total` items over `parts` owners.\nvoid partition(const size_t total, const int parts, const int idx,\n               size_t& begin, size_t& count) {\n    const size_t base = total / parts;\n    const size_t rem = total % parts;\n    const size_t u = static_cast<size_t>(idx);\n    begin = u * base + std::min(u, rem);\n    count = base + (u < rem ? 1 : 0);\n}\n\n// Ranks sharing a node split its GPUs; if ranks outnumber GPUs, ranks share round-robin.\nstd::vector<int> devicesForRank(const int localRank, const int localSize, const int numDevices) {\n    std::vector<int> devs;\n    if (localSize <= numDevices) {\n        for (int d = localRank; d < numDevices; d += localSize) devs.push_back(d);\n    } else {\n        devs.push_back(localRank % numDevices);\n    }\n    return devs;\n}\n\n// Create CUDA contexts up front so context setup is not part of the timed region.\nvoid warmUpDevices(const std::vector<int>& devs) {\n    const int nd = static_cast<int>(devs.size());\n    #pragma omp parallel for num_threads(nd) schedule(static, 1)\n    for (int t = 0; t < nd; ++t) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(devs[t]));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n    }\n}\n\n// Compute the local rows of C (m x N) = hA (m x N) * hB (N x N) using all devices of this rank.\nvoid multiplyLocalRows(const double* hA, const double* hB, double* hC,\n                       const size_t m, const size_t N, const std::vector<int>& devs) {\n    const int nd = static_cast<int>(devs.size());\n    #pragma omp parallel for num_threads(nd) schedule(static, 1)\n    for (int t = 0; t < nd; ++t) {\n        size_t rowBegin = 0, rowCount = 0;\n        partition(m, nd, t, rowBegin, rowCount);\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(devs[t]));\n        if (rowCount == 0 || N == 0) continue;\n\n        const size_t aBytes = rowCount * N * sizeof(double);\n        const size_t bBytes = N * N * sizeof(double);\n\n        double *dA = nullptr, *dB = nullptr, *dC = nullptr;\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dA, aBytes));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dB, bBytes));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dC, aBytes));\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dA, hA + rowBegin * N, aBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dB, hB, bBytes, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n        const dim3 block(BN / TN, BM / TM);\n        const dim3 grid(static_cast<unsigned>((N + BN - 1) / BN),\n                        static_cast<unsigned>((rowCount + BM - 1) / BM));\n        matmulTiled<<<grid, block>>>(dA, dB, dC, static_cast<int>(rowCount), static_cast<int>(N));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n        // Synchronous copy-back also waits for the kernel to finish.\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(hC + rowBegin * N, dC, aBytes, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dA));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dB));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dC));\n    }\n}\n\n// Simple validation: compute a few elements on the host and compare.\n// A and B are regenerated on demand (identical values to the initialized matrices).\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& C, const size_t N) {\n    // Check a few random positions\n    constexpr size_t checkPoints[] = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4};\n\n    for (size_t pi = 0; pi < 5; ++pi) {\n        for (size_t pj = 0; pj < 5; ++pj) {\n            const size_t i = checkPoints[pi] % N;\n            const size_t j = checkPoints[pj] % N;\n\n            double expected = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < N; ++k) {\n                expected += getPseudoRndValue(N, i, k) * getPseudoRndValue(N, k, j);\n            }\n\n            const double actual = C[i * N + j];\n            const double relError = std::abs((actual - expected) / (expected + 1e-10));\n\n            if (relError > 1e-6) {\n                printf(\"Validation failed at (%zu, %zu): expected %.10f, got %.10f (error: %.10e)\\n\",\n                       i, j, expected, actual, relError);\n                return false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size N (computes NxN * NxN) (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint runBenchmark(int argc, char** argv, const int rank, const int size) {\n    size_t N = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            N = if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            if (rank == 0) printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            if (rank == 0) {\n                printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n                printUsage(argv[0]);\n            }\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Matrix Multiplication Benchmark\\n\");\n MPI_Comm localComm;\n    MPI_Comm_split_type(MPI_COMM_WORLD, MPI_COMM_TYPE_SHARED, rank, MPI_INFO_NULL, &localComm);\n    int localRank = 0, localSize = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(localComm, &localRank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(localComm, &localSize);\n    MPI_Comm_free(&localComm);\n\n    int numDevices = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&numDevices));\n    if (numDevices == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"Rank %d: no CUDA devices available\\n\", rank);\n        MPI_Abort(MPI_COMM_WORLD, 1);\n    }\n    const std::vector<int> devs = devicesForRank(localRank, localSize, numDevices);\n\n    // Row block owned by this rank.\n    size_t rowBegin = 0, rowCount = 0;\n    partition(N, size, rank, rowBegin, rowCount);\n\n    // Allocate and initialize local data\n    if (rank == 0) printf(\"Initializing matrices...\\n\");\n    std::vector<double> A(rowCount * N);\n    std::vector<double> B(N * N);\n    std::vector<double> C(rowCount * N);\n    initRows(A.data(), N, rowBegin, rowCount);\n    initRows(B.data(), N, 0, N);\n\n    // Perform matrix multiplication\n    if (rank == 0) printf(\"Computing matrix multiplication...\\n\");\n    warmUpDevices(devs);\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    multiplyLocalRows(A.data(), B.data(), C.data(), rowCount, N, devs);\n\n    MPI_Barrier(MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    int ret = 0;\n    if (rank == 0) {\n        printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n        // Calculate GFLOPS\n        double gflops = (2.0 * N * N * N) / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n        printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    }\n\n    // Gather full C on rank 0 only when it is needed for output or validation.\n    if (printResults || validate) {\n        std::vector<int> counts(size), displs(size);\n        for (int r = 0; r < size; ++r) {\n            size_t rb = 0, rc = 0;\n            partition(N, size, r, rb, rc);\n            counts[r] = }\n\n    // Keep the exit status consistent across all ranks.\n    MPI_Bcast(&ret, 1, MPI_INT, 0, MPI_COMM_WORLD);\n    return ret;\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    MPI_Init(&argc, &argv);\n\n    int rank = 0, size = 1;\n    MPI_Comm_rank(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &rank);\n    MPI_Comm_size(MPI_COMM_WORLD, &size);\n\n    const int ret = runBenchmark(argc, argv, rank, size);\n\n {"type":"step_start","timestamp":1793047829602,"sessionID":"ses_e8609575affeVu0Ptqg56NiOxK","part":{"id":"prt_179fa9c5c0018s3uePEywPQCaA","messageID":"msg_179fa9638001KL0HeczVOgKfjo","sessionID":"ses_e8609575affeVu0Ptqg56NiOxK","type":"step-start"}}
{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793047839807,"sessionID":"ses_e8609575affeVu0Ptqg56NiOxK","part":{"id":"prt_179fa9c5f001PJ7o4SqV0xljQj","messageID":"msg_179fa9638001KL0HeczVOgKfjo","sessionID":"ses_e8609575affeVu0Ptqg56NiOxK","type":"reasoning","text":"I'm noticing GCC actually vectorized the k-loop into 2-wide SIMD lanes, multiplying pairs of doubles and summing them separately before combining—which is odd since without -ffast-math it shouldn't be reassociating the reduction like that.\n\nSo it preserves sequential order (sum = (sum + p0) + p1), but the multiply and add stay unfused except for one spot: when N is odd, the leftover tail element gets handled by a fused vfmadd instruction, while all the vectorized pairs use separate multiply/add. That means my test with N=7 happened to match the \"non-fused\" result because the single fused tail element didn't shift the final rounding compared to the fully non-fused version, even though it technically used FMA.\n\nSince the original's exact fusing/ordering depends on GCC's vectorization choices and varies by stride and parity, matching it bit-exact across all N requires replicating this same mixed fused/non-fused pattern rather than picking one uniform approach.\n\nGiven the uncertainty, I'll test empirically: simulate the no-FMA-for-all-k hypothesis against known samples. For N=7 it matches the observed value, but I need to verify this holds across other N sizes before committing to it as the semantic to replicate.\n\nTo confirm, I should build the original code with fused-multiply-add explicitly disabled and compare hashes for several N values — if they match across odd and even cases, that confirms the non-fused sequential interpretation, and I can mirror that same flag behavior on the GPU side.\n\n","time":{"start":1793047829599,"end":1793047839801},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

I should verify this by constructing a reference implementation that sums non-fused for all but the last term when N is odd, fusing only that final term.\n\nFor the GPU kernel, the goal is to replicate this exact behavior — using plain multiply-add except fusing the last term when N is odd, compiled with FMA contraction disabled so nothing else fuses unexpectedly. Still, I'm weighing whether bit-exact matching of this GCC quirk is actually the right target versus just accepting FMA throughout for better precision.\n\nThere's a real performance cost here since double-precision is already throughput-limited, so splitting multiply and add instead of fusing roughly doubles the work on that pipeline. But since correctness is being judged against the original's exact output, matching the non-fused behavior is the safer choice even with that tradeoff, since fusion would genuinely change the final bits.\n\nThe compiler's treatment of the odd-N tail element is implementation-specific, so I'll match the default build behavior and document the assumption. For ordering, I confirm the pairwise lane additions happen sequentially (lane0 then lane1), matching the original's unpckhpd pattern.\n\nWriting the kernel logic to special-case the final k-index when N is odd, using fused multiply-add only there while the rest of the accumulation stays as separate multiply and add steps...\n\nI should verify the explicit `__dadd_rn`/`__dmul_rn` intrinsics avoid unwanted fused-multiply-add contraction regardless of nvcc's default fmad setting, and that both host-side glibc fma and device fma() are correctly rounded so validation tolerance of 1e-6 covers any discrepancies. I'll plan to test the implementation against the original across many N values (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 64, 65, 100, 333, 1000) including multi-rank and multi-GPU cases, then proceed to edit the kernel.\n\n","time":{"start":1793047867045,"end":1793047878772},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
